sentences.en: And to cut a very long story short, this war, the War of 1812, broke out that summer for four reasons.
sentences.zh: 长话短说，这场战争，即1812年战争，由于四个原因在当年夏天爆发了。

sentences.en: So first of all, the Madison administration.
sentences.zh: 首先，麦迪逊政府。

sentences.en: So this is, I think, the fourth president of the United States, James Madison, not a terribly colourful or well-known president.
sentences.zh: 我想这是美国第四任总统詹姆斯·麦迪逊，并不是一位个性鲜明或广为人知的总统。

sentences.en: He's chafing at Britain's trade embargo against Napoleonic France.
sentences.zh: 他对英国针对拿破仑法国的贸易禁运感到恼火。

sentences.en: And the Americans say, come on, why are we subject to this trade embargo?
sentences.zh: 美国人说，拜托，我们凭什么要遭受这种贸易禁运？

sentences.en: We want to be able to trade freely.
sentences.zh: 我们想要能够自由贸易。

sentences.en: We don't want the Royal Navy, you know, seizing our ships.
sentences.zh: 我们不想让皇家海军扣押我们的船只。

sentences.en: Reason number two, they don't want the Royal Navy pressing American seamen into the Royal Navy.
sentences.zh: 第二个原因，他们不希望皇家海军将美国海员强征入皇家海军服役。

sentences.en: So when the Royal Navy, you know, sees an American ship, they will take some of the Americans and force them to work on the British ship.
sentences.zh: 所以当皇家海军看到一艘美国船时，他们会带走一些美国人，强迫他们在英国船上干活。

sentences.en: People are sick of that.
sentences.zh: 人们对此已经厌烦透顶。

sentences.en: Number three, the Madison administration have expansionist ambitions.
sentences.zh: 第三点，麦迪逊政府有着扩张主义的野心。

sentences.en: So they think, or the Brits are just distracted by what's going on in Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为，英国人正被欧洲发生的事情分散了注意力。

sentences.en: We can seize upper and lower Canada.

sentences.en: So that's sort of Ontario country.

sentences.en: And that's something they've been kind of angling to do since the War of Independence, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是他们自独立战争以来一直渴望做的事，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly, they have.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，他们确实如此。

sentences.en: They think they've got unfinished business, basically.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己基本上还有未竟的事业。

sentences.en: They want to take what becomes Canada.
sentences.zh: 他们想夺取后来成为加拿大的领土。

sentences.en: And it kind of rumbles on, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 而且这事一直断断续续地闹着，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 因为还有关于风车的那档子事。

sentences.en: Great Canadian victory.

sentences.en: And the Americans also think there are lots of sort of Native American Indian confederations that stand in the way of westward expansion that are allied to the British.
sentences.zh: 美国人还认为，有许多美洲印第安人部落联盟阻碍了他们向西扩张，而这些部落与英国人结盟了。

sentences.en: Let's seize the opportunity to knock them out, too.
sentences.zh: 让我们抓住机会把他们也干掉吧。

sentences.en: And finally, they think, you know, nothing builds a nation more than a war, a successful war.
sentences.zh: 最后，他们认为，没有什么比一场战争、一场胜利的战争更能凝聚一个国家了。

sentences.zh: 所以这是对英爱协同作战的一次提醒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Ireland and Great Britain standing shoulder to shoulder against a common foe.
sentences.zh: 爱尔兰和英国并肩作战，共同抗击共同的敌人。

sentences.en: I think that's how we like to see it.
sentences.zh: 我想我们更愿意这样来看待它。

sentences.en: Heartwarming.
sentences.zh: 真温馨。

sentences.en: So they burn the White House, they eat Dolly Madison's dinner, and four days later, they are heading for their next target, which is Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 于是他们烧了白宫，吃了多莉·麦迪逊的晚宴，四天后，他们正朝着下一个目标进发，那就是巴尔的摩。

sentences.en: Baltimore, Maryland, at this point, is, I think, something like the third biggest city in the United States.
sentences.zh: 当时的马里兰州巴尔的摩，我想大概是美国第三大城市。

sentences.en: It's a really important trading hub and harbour and all of that.
sentences.zh: 它是一个极其重要的贸易枢纽、港口以及诸如此类的地方。

sentences.en: And they are in great spirits, the British.
sentences.zh: 英国人情绪高涨。

sentences.en: They've been drinking a lot, unsurprisingly, and they've been helping themselves to what they see as long overdue tax returns from the American rebels.
sentences.zh: 毫不意外，他们喝了很多酒，而且一直在拿他们眼中美国叛军“拖欠已久的税款”来犒劳自己。

sentences.en: And sad to say, there's a local busybody who's called Dr. Beans, Dr. William Beans, and he lives in rural Maryland.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是，当地有一个好管闲事的人叫豆子医生，即威廉·豆子医生，他住在马里兰州的乡村。

sentences.en: He tries to stop the British from basically looting and pillaging.
sentences.zh: 他试图阻止英国人进行大肆的搜刮和掠夺。

sentences.en: They're not looting and pillaging.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有在搜刮掠夺。

sentences.en: You just said they're collecting tax arrears.
sentences.zh: 你刚才说他们在收缴拖欠的税款。

sentences.en: That was just me putting myself in Dr. Beans's head.
sentences.zh: 那只是我把自己代入了比恩斯医生的视角。

sentences.en: I don't agree with him.
sentences.zh: 我并不同意他的做法。

sentences.en: He's obviously a terrible man.
sentences.zh: 他显然是个糟糕的家伙。

sentences.en: Oh, thank God I'm on hand to provide the objectivity that a good history podcast should provide.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢天谢地，我能提供一份优秀的播客应有的客观视角。

sentences.en: So, quite rightly, our brave lads arrested this bloke, Beans, and they took him down the river towards Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的勇士们理所当然地逮捕了这个叫比恩斯的家伙，并把他顺着河带向巴尔的摩。

sentences.en: And some of his friends wanted to petition the British for Dr. Beans's release.
sentences.zh: 他的一些朋友想要向英国人请愿，要求释放比恩斯医生。

sentences.en: This was a very common practice during the war.
sentences.zh: 这在当时是非常普遍的做法。

sentences.en: He would basically go under flag of truce and say, please, can we have so-and-so back?
sentences.zh: 他基本上会打着休战的旗号去说，拜托，能把某某还给我们吗？

sentences.en: And his friends decide to get a go-between, and the go-between in question is a lawyer called Francis Scott Key.
sentences.zh: 他的朋友们决定找一个中间人，而这个中间人是一个名叫弗朗西斯·斯科特·基的律师。

sentences.en: Who we mentioned right at the start of this show.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目一开始就提到过他。

sentences.en: We did, indeed.
sentences.zh: 我们的确提过。

sentences.en: So, he's the author of the anthem.
sentences.zh: 所以，他是国歌的词作者。

sentences.en: Now, American listeners, of course, will recognize his name, but they might not know loads about him.
sentences.zh: 当然，美国听众会认出他的名字，但他们可能对他的了解并不多。

sentences.en: Key was born in 1779 to a fairly well-oiled family in Maryland.
sentences.zh: 基出生于1779年，出自马里兰州一个相当富裕的家庭。

sentences.en: His father had been in George Washington's rebel army.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲曾是乔治·华盛顿的叛军军队成员。

sentences.en: He'd been a judge.
sentences.zh: 他曾担任过法官。

sentences.en: Francis Scott Key grew up in the family plantation.
sentences.zh: 弗朗西斯·斯科特·基是在家族种植园里长大的。

sentences.en: So, he's from a slave-owning family.
sentences.zh: 所以，他出身于一个蓄奴家庭。

sentences.en: He comes from a slave-owning family, which will be important later on.
sentences.zh: 他出身于一个蓄奴家庭，这在后来会很重要。

sentences.en: He was a well-known lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他是一位知名的律师。

sentences.en: He had 11 children, which I think seems a lot.
sentences.zh: 他有11个孩子，我觉得这听起来很多。

sentences.en: He lives with his wife and 11 children in Georgetown.
sentences.zh: 他和妻子以及11个孩子住在乔治敦。

sentences.en: He does various big trials.
sentences.zh: 他接手过各种大案。

sentences.en: He speaks before the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 他在最高法院进行辩论。

sentences.en: He's quite a well-known person.
sentences.zh: 他是个相当知名的人物。

sentences.en: And the fact that he is a slave owner, Tom, I'm glad you've flagged it, because it is going to make this anthem controversial later on.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，鉴于他是个蓄奴者，我很高兴你指出了这一点，因为这会让这首国歌在后来备受争议。

sentences.en: So, we'll come to that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们等下会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: Anyway, the 2nd of September, 1814, Key writes to his mother, and he says,
sentences.zh: 总之，在1814年9月2日，基写信给他的母亲，他说，

sentences.en: I'm going in the morning to Baltimore to proceed in a flag vessel to General Ross.
sentences.zh: 我早上要去巴尔的摩，乘一艘停战船前往罗斯将军那里。

sentences.en: Old Dr. Beans of Marlborough is taken prisoner by the enemy.
sentences.zh: 万宝路的长老比恩斯被敌人俘虏了。

sentences.en: And some of his friends have urged me to go and get him out and to procure his release.
sentences.zh: 他的一些朋友敦促我去把他救出来并争取他的释放。

sentences.en: I don't know where he is, but I'll do my beSt.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他在哪儿，但我会尽力而为。

sentences.en: So, he goes off to Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 于是，他动身前往巴尔的摩。

sentences.en: He finds the local United States agent who deals with prisoners of war.
sentences.zh: 他找到了负责处理战俘事务的当地美国代理人。

sentences.en: They rent a ship, and they sail off towards Chesapeake Bay, and they're looking for the
sentences.zh: 他们租了一艘船，驶向切萨皮克湾，寻找

sentences.en: British fleet, because they think that's where this bloke Beans is being held.
sentences.zh: 英国舰队，因为他们认为那个叫比恩斯的家伙被关在那里。

sentences.en: And on the 7th of September, they find HMS Tonant near the mouth of the Potomac in Chesapeake Bay.
sentences.zh: 9月7日，他们在切萨皮克湾波托马克河口附近找到了“特纳”号战舰。

sentences.en: Now, some people may remember HMS Tonant, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，有些人可能还记得“特纳”号战舰。

sentences.en: Do you remember it?
sentences.zh: 你还记得吗？

sentences.en: That's the question.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: Well, the name is, of course, the French one.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个名字当然是法文名字。

sentences.en: And we have done a series on a particular British admiral who's very good at capturing
sentences.zh: 我们做过一个系列节目，讲的是一位特别擅长俘获

sentences.en: French ships.
sentences.zh: 法国船只的英国海军上将。

sentences.en: We have.
sentences.zh: 我们确实做过。

sentences.en: Now, can anyone remember the name of that admiral?
sentences.zh: 现在，有人还记得那位海军上将的名字吗？

sentences.en: Is it Admiral Nelson?
sentences.zh: 是纳尔逊海军上将吗？

sentences.en: It is!
sentences.zh: 正是！

sentences.en: Superb.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: So, Tonant had been captured at the Nile.
sentences.zh: 所以，“特纳”号是在尼罗河战役中被俘的。

sentences.en: It had fought splendidly under Captain Charles Tyler at Trafalgar.
sentences.zh: 它在查尔斯·泰勒船长的指挥下，在特拉法尔加战役中英勇作战。

sentences.en: It had captured a French ship, and now the Tonant is fighting the Americans.
sentences.zh: 它俘获过一艘法国船，现在“特纳”号正在与美国人作战。

sentences.en: Anyway, so Key approaches the Tonant under flag of truce, and he's allowed aboard.
sentences.zh: 总之，基打着停战旗接近了“特纳”号，并获准登船。

sentences.en: He and this agent that he's with, they are invited for dinner by the British.
sentences.zh: 他和同行的这位代理人受到了英国人的晚餐邀请。

sentences.en: They're treated very well, the British bigwigs.
sentences.zh: 英国大人物们对他们礼遇有加。

sentences.en: Well, because Ross, the Irishman, has a tremendous reputation for chivalry.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为那个爱尔兰人罗斯以骑士精神闻名遐迩。

sentences.en: Very chivalrous.
sentences.zh: 非常具有骑士风度。

sentences.en: Charming man.
sentences.zh: 是个迷人的人。

sentences.en: So, when they say to Ross, can we have this bloke, Dr. Beans?
sentences.zh: 所以，当他们对罗斯说，我们能把比恩斯医生带走吗？

sentences.en: Ross says, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 罗斯说，我不知道。

sentences.en: And Key has brought letters from wounded British soldiers, British prisoners of war, saying that American doctors as a group have been very kind to them.
sentences.zh: 基带来了受伤的英国士兵和英国战俘的信件，信中说美国医生总体对他们非常好。

sentences.en: And Ross reads these letters, and he says, oh, well, okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 罗斯读了这些信，然后说，哦，好吧，行吧。

sentences.en: You can have, you know, maybe Beans can go.
sentences.zh: 你们可以带走……你知道的，也许比恩斯可以走。

sentences.en: Because he's a warm-hearted man.
sentences.zh: 因为他是个热心肠的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, kindly.
sentences.zh: 是的，很善良。

sentences.en: So, it looks like they're just going to go about with this bloke, Beans.
sentences.zh: 所以，看起来他们就要带着这个叫比恩斯的家伙一起离开了。

sentences.en: However, while they've been having dinner, the Americans have overheard the British officers talking about how they're going to attack Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 然而，就在他们享用晚餐时，美国人无意中听到英国军官在讨论他们将如何进攻巴尔的摩。

sentences.en: And so, the British say, well, since you've heard us talking about this, you're going to have to stay with us until the operation is over.
sentences.zh: 于是，英国人说，既然你们听到了我们的讨论，那你们就得留下来，直到行动结束。

sentences.en: And so, Key and Beans are transferred to another ship, HMS Surprise, which is towing the little ship that they'd arrived on.
sentences.zh: 因此，基和比恩斯被转移到了另一艘船上，即“惊奇”号，该船正拖着他们到达时乘坐的小船。

sentences.en: And they all move together up the Chesapeake towards Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 他们一起顺着切萨皮克湾向巴尔的摩驶去。

sentences.en: And on the 11th, the Americans are allowed to go back to their own ship, which is still tethered to HMS Surprise.
sentences.zh: 11日，美国人被允许返回他们自己的船上，该船仍然拴在“惊奇”号上。

sentences.en: And they're basically under military guard.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上处于军事监视之下。

sentences.en: The 12th, nothing happens.
sentences.zh: 12日，什么也没发生。

sentences.en: They're just hanging around, a bit bored.
sentences.zh: 他们只是闲逛，觉得有点无聊。

sentences.en: And then at dawn on the 13th, the British open the bombardment of Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 然后，在13日黎明时分，英国人对巴尔的摩发动了轰炸。

sentences.en: Or more specifically, they open the bombardment of the fort that guards the entrance to Baltimore
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，他们轰炸的是守卫巴尔的摩港入口的要塞

sentences.en: Harbour, which is Fort McHenry, which is the fort in the anthem.
sentences.zh: ——麦克亨利堡，也就是国歌中提到的那个要塞。

sentences.en: So, Key and this medical busybody, this massive fun sponge, Dr. Beans, who's been trying to stop our brave lads looting, they're watching this from a safe distance on their ship.
sentences.zh: 所以，基和这个好管闲事的医生、这个超级扫兴鬼比恩斯——他之前一直试图阻止我们的勇士们掠夺——正从他们船上的安全距离外观看着这一切。

sentences.en: They're about eight miles away.
sentences.zh: 他们大约在八英里外。

sentences.en: And they can see that this bombardment is a really big deal.
sentences.zh: 他们能看出这场轰炸绝非小事。

sentences.en: So, the attack is led by HMS Erebus, which is firing Congreve rockets.
sentences.zh: 进攻由“厄瑞波斯”号战舰带头，它发射了康格里夫火箭。

sentences.en: So, if you know the American national anthem, the rockets' red glare, these are the Congreve rockets being fired by HMS Erebus.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你知道美国国歌，那句“火箭的红光”，这就是“厄瑞波斯”号发射的康格里夫火箭。

sentences.en: I mean, they're dangerous, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们很危险，对吧？

sentences.en: They're very dangerous.
sentences.zh: 它们非常危险。

sentences.en: They basically, the British use them to burn down Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 英国人基本上是用它们来烧毁哥本哈根的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, anyone who remembers our Nelson-era podcasts will remember that, you know, naval bombardments are not a bundle of laughs.
sentences.zh: 你知道，任何还记得我们纳尔逊时期播客的人都会记得，海军轰炸可绝不是什么好玩的事。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, there are, just as at Copenhagen, there are also bomb vessels, specialist bomb vessels.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像在哥本哈根一样，这里也有轰炸船，专门的轰炸船。

sentences.en: So, in this case, they're called Terror, Volcano, Devastation, Meteor, and Etna.
sentences.zh: 在这个案子里，它们的名字叫“恐怖”号、“火山”号、“毁灭”号、“流星”号和“埃特纳”号。

sentences.en: God, you wouldn't want to be attacked by ships with names like that.
sentences.zh: 天哪，你可不想遭到名字这么吓人的船只攻击。

sentences.en: You wouldn't.
sentences.zh: 确实不想。

sentences.en: Do we still have ships like that in the Royal Navy?
sentences.zh: 英国皇家海军现在还有这样的船吗？

sentences.en: I don't think we do.
sentences.zh: 我想我们没有了吧。

sentences.en: No, we don't have any ships, do we?
sentences.zh: 对，我们没有什么船了，对吧？

sentences.en: No, we don't have any ships.
sentences.zh: 不，我们没有什么船了。

sentences.en: These ships are firing shells at the fort, and these are the bombs bursting in air from the anthem.
sentences.zh: 这些船正向要塞发射炮弹，这就是国歌中“空中炸裂的炸弹”的来源。

sentences.en: And over the next 24 hours or so, they fire a total of 700 rockets, 1,500 shells.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的大约24小时里，他们总共发射了700枚火箭弹和1500枚炮弹。

sentences.en: However, although you quake at the thought of these rockets and shells, Tom, they're not
sentences.zh: 然而，汤姆，尽管你一想到这些火箭弹和炮弹就胆战心惊，但它们

sentences.en: very effective, because Fort McHenry is equipped with very powerful artillery, so the British have to stay back at the very limit of their range, and they don't really do that much
sentences.zh: 并不是很有效，因为麦克亨利堡装备了威力巨大的火炮，所以英国人不得不退到他们射程的极限边缘，实际上并没有造成那么大的

sentences.en: damage.
sentences.zh: 破坏。

sentences.en: They kill four people, they wound 24, but they don't really have any impact whatsoever on the fort's defences.
sentences.zh: 他们炸死了4个人，炸伤了24人，但对要塞的防御工事没有产生任何实质性的影响。

sentences.en: I wonder what Nelson would have done.
sentences.zh: 我想知道纳尔逊会怎么做。

sentences.en: He would have launched an operation at land that would have involved him losing an arm, surely.
sentences.zh: 他肯定会发起一场陆上行动，代价是失去一只胳膊。

sentences.en: Falling in love with an unsuitable American adventurer.
sentences.zh: 爱上一个不合适的美国冒险家。

sentences.en: There's a good historical novel in that.
sentences.zh: 这倒是个很好的历史小说题材。

sentences.en: Anyway, Key, Francis Scott Key, is watching this.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，基——弗朗西斯·斯科特·基正在看着这一切。

sentences.en: He can't tell that they're not having any effect.
sentences.zh: 他看不出对方其实并没有造成什么影响。

sentences.en: He's just in awe at the general spectacle.
sentences.zh: 他只是对眼前的壮观景象惊叹不已。

sentences.en: It seemed as though Mother Earth had opened and was vomiting shot and shell and a sheet of fire and brimstone, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，这情景看起来就像大地裂开，喷吐着枪林弹雨以及一片烈火和硫磺。

sentences.en: Anyway, darkness falls.
sentences.zh: 总之，夜幕降临了。

sentences.en: There's just this kind of vague red blur in the distance.
sentences.zh: 远处只剩下一片模糊的红色光晕。

sentences.en: More stuff is exploding on the walls of the fort.
sentences.zh: 更多的东西在要塞的城墙上爆炸。

sentences.en: Basically, he, all night, he's kind of watching this and he's thinking, like, has the fort fallen?
sentences.zh: 基本上，他整晚都在看着这一切，心里想，要塞失守了吗？

sentences.en: You know, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 你知道，到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Because he's not a military man.
sentences.zh: 因为他不是个军人。

sentences.en: So he doesn't appreciate that the British Navy is operating sportingly at the limits of what it can actually do.
sentences.zh: 所以他并不理解英国海军是在其作战能力的极限边缘进行一场堂吉诃德式的尝试。

sentences.en: Dawn breaks on the 14th and the fort still stands.
sentences.zh: 14日黎明破晓，要塞依然屹立。

sentences.en: And as every morning, the American commander, Major George Armistead, orders his men to raise
sentences.zh: 和每天早上一样，美国指挥官乔治·阿米斯特德少校命令他的手下升起

sentences.en: this massive national flag, which, as you said at the beginning, has 15 stars and 15 stripes.
sentences.zh: 这面巨大的国旗，正如你一开始所说，它有15颗星和15道条纹。

sentences.en: Now, this flag, which is now in the Smithsonian, actually, this flag has a history of its own.
sentences.zh: 现在这面旗帜其实正保存在史密森尼博物馆里，它有着自己的历史。

sentences.en: So a year earlier, Major Armistead had actually said, you know, the British are probably going to attack Baltimore.
sentences.zh: 就在一年前，阿米斯特德少校实际上还说过，你知道，英国人可能会进攻巴尔的摩。

sentences.en: We need a bloody big flag.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一面超大的旗帜。

sentences.en: We want to have a flag so large that the British will have no difficulty seeing it from a distance.
sentences.zh: 我们要一面大到让英国人老远就能一眼看清的旗帜。

sentences.en: So he basically wanted this flag as a sort of emblem of defiance.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上想要这面旗帜作为一种挑衅的象征。

sentences.en: And he commissioned the flag, which is absolutely massive.
sentences.zh: 他定制了这面绝对巨大的旗帜。

sentences.en: It's 42 feet by 30 feet.
sentences.zh: 它有42英尺长，30英尺宽。

sentences.en: He commissioned it from a Baltimore widow called Mary Pickersgill.
sentences.zh: 他向巴尔的摩一位名叫玛丽·皮克斯吉尔的寡妇订制了它。

sentences.en: And she took her six weeks to make it.
sentences.zh: 她花了六个星期才把它做完。

sentences.en: She made it with her teenage daughter and her nieces and a servant.
sentences.zh: 她和她的十几岁的女儿、几个侄女以及一个仆人一起制作了它。

sentences.en: I don't want to do this.
sentences.zh: 我才不想做这个。

sentences.en: Ugh, so boring.

sentences.zh: 基本上，街头民谣的意思是，你根据一首非常熟悉的曲调来创作歌词或诗歌。

sentences.en: In the first half, we described how George Coburn's objective was to raid and destroy the towns and harbours on the Atlantic seaboard.
sentences.zh: 在前半部分中，我们描述了乔治·科伯恩的目标是突袭并摧毁大西洋沿岸的城镇和港口。

sentences.en: To guide his raiding parties, he needed local intelligence.
sentences.zh: 为了给他的突袭部队引路，他需要当地的情报。

sentences.en: And from the moment he arrived in 1813, he and the other British captains relied on one group above all, which was escaped slaves.
sentences.zh: 从他1813年抵达的那一刻起，他和英国的其他船长们主要依赖一个群体，那就是逃亡奴隶。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that, again, is something that goes back to the American War of Independence, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这又是一个可以追溯到美国独立战争的事情，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because this was a British strategy to offer slaves in the South their freedom if they would join the British.
sentences.zh: 因为这是英国的一项战略，即向南方的奴隶提供自由，条件是他们加入英国。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So at first, British ships and British parties would attract individual runaway slaves.
sentences.zh: 所以起初，英国船只和英国队伍会吸引个别的逃亡奴隶。

sentences.en: But over time, they start to attract larger groups and family groups and so on.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，他们开始吸引更大的群体、家庭群体等等。

sentences.en: And when Coburn came back in 1814, he'd been wintering in Bermuda, but then he comes back.
sentences.zh: 当科伯恩在1814年回来时，他一直在百慕大过冬，然后他回来了。

sentences.en: He doubled down on this and he said to his captains, I want you to go out of your way to appeal to the local slave population.
sentences.zh: 他加倍执行这一策略，并对他的船长们说，我希望你们不遗余力地去吸引当地的黑人人口。

sentences.en: And I quote, let the landings you make be more for the protection of the desertion of the black population than with a view to any other advantage.
sentences.zh: 我引用原话：你们发动的登陆行动，与其说是为了谋取其他利益，不如说是为了保护和接纳黑人人口的逃亡。

sentences.en: The great point to be attained is the cordial support of the black population.
sentences.zh: 要达到的主要目标是获得黑人人口的衷心支持。

sentences.en: With them properly armed and back to 20,000 British troops, Mr. Madison will be hurled from his throne.
sentences.zh: 只要妥善武装他们，并有两万英军作后盾，麦迪逊先生就会被赶下台。

sentences.en: And as part of this, he makes a very specific promise.
sentences.zh: 作为其中的一部分，他做出了一个非常具体的承诺。

sentences.en: All runaway slaves will be welcomed by the British and under no circumstances will they be handed back.
sentences.zh: 所有逃亡的奴隶都将受到英国人的欢迎，并且在任何情况下都不会被遣返。

sentences.en: When the British tried this policy in the American War of Independence,
sentences.zh: 当英国人在美国独立战争期间尝试这一政策时，

sentences.en: it was obviously massively compromised because the British themselves were defending the plantations in the Caribbean on which there were slaves.
sentences.zh: 它显然遭到了极大的削弱，因为英国人自己也在加勒比海保卫那些拥有奴隶的种植园。

sentences.en: Slavery was not illegal.
sentences.zh: 当时奴隶制并非非法。

sentences.en: By this point, you have a British foreign secretary who is about to go to the Congress of Vienna and press for the abolition of the slave trade with the other great powers.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，你有一位英国外交大臣，他即将前往维也纳会议，并敦促其他大国废除奴隶贸易。

sentences.en: Is that something you think that would have filtered through to black Americans?
sentences.zh: 你认为这件事会传到黑人美国人的耳朵里吗？

sentences.en: Very hard to say because you wouldn't really have, you wouldn't find much textual evidence.
sentences.zh: 这很难说，因为你不会真正拥有、也不会找到太多的文字证据。

sentences.en: Yeah, how would you find it?
sentences.zh: 对啊，你怎么可能找得到呢？

sentences.en: But maybe it's just kind of, you know, it's on the grapevine.
sentences.zh: 但也许它只是那种，你知道的，通过小道消息传播的。

sentences.en: I mean, it would be big news, I would imagine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想这会是大新闻。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's possible.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是有可能的。

sentences.en: The British government has turned abolitioniSt.
sentences.zh: 英国政府已经变成了废奴主义者。

sentences.en: There is absolutely no doubt that the news of what he is offering does, you know, filter through.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，他所提供的条件的消息确实，你知道的，渗透了进来。

sentences.en: And yes, you could well imagine people saying, well, the British have already talked about scrapping it.
sentences.zh: 是的，你可以想象人们会说，英国人已经讨论过废除它了。

sentences.en: And what actually he does that really horrifies white American opinion, he says,
sentences.zh: 而他实际采取的行动却让白人美国舆论感到极度惊恐，他说，

sentences.en: All male runaway slaves will be armed, they will be given red uniforms, and they will be put in a special unit called the Corps of Colonial Marines.
sentences.zh: 所有逃亡的男奴都将被武装起来，发给他们红色军服，并将他们编入一个名为“殖民地海军陆战队”的特殊部队。

sentences.en: Yeah, because this is the nightmare that haunted the original Ku Klux Klan, isn't it, in that series that we did after the Civil War.
sentences.zh: 对，因为这就是我们在内战后制作的那部纪录片系列中，困扰最初三K党的噩梦，不是吗？

sentences.en: Nothing ever frightens white Southern slaveholders more than the prospect of armed black men, you know, rising up against them or being emboldened against them.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比武装黑人男子，你知道的，对他们进行反抗或受到鼓舞的前景，更能吓坏南方白人奴隶主的了。

sentences.en: Anyway, this Corps of Colonial Marines did see action.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，这支殖民地海军陆战队确实参与了战斗。

sentences.en: They went into battle in Virginia in the end of May, and they did really well.
sentences.zh: 他们在五月底进入弗吉尼亚参战，而且表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: Their British officers said, I was highly pleased by the conduct of the Colonial Marines,
sentences.zh: 他们的英国军官说，我对殖民地海军陆战队的表现感到非常满意，

sentences.en: every individual of which evinced the greatest eagerness to come to action with their former masters.
sentences.zh: 其中的每一个人都表现出极大的渴望，要与他们以前的主人交战。

sentences.en: And Coburn himself wrote, they trigger the most general and undisguised alarm among American civilians.
sentences.zh: 科伯恩自己也写道，他们在美国平民中引发了最普遍、最毫不掩饰的恐慌。

sentences.en: There were even former slaves involved in the burning of Washington, which must have been sweet revenge for them, you would guess.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有前奴隶参与了火烧华盛顿，你可以猜到，这对外他们来说一定是大快人心的复仇。

sentences.en: Anyway, the Americans, by contrast, think this is absolutely terrible.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，与此相对，美国人认为这绝对太糟糕了。

sentences.en: They think it's an outrage.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一种令人发指的行为。

sentences.en: They think it's cheating.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是作弊。

sentences.en: But they think it's more than cheating.
sentences.zh: 但他们认为这不仅仅是作弊。

sentences.en: They think it's an affront to the laws of God and of nature to arm their former slaves against them.
sentences.zh: 他们认为武装前奴隶来对付他们是对上帝和自然律的侮辱。

sentences.en: One senior officer writes in August 1814,
sentences.zh: 一位高级军官在1814年8月写道，

sentences.en: Our Negroes are flocking to the enemy from all quarters, which they convert into troops vindictive and rapacious with the most minute knowledge of every by-path.
sentences.zh: 我们的黑奴正从四面八方涌向敌人，敌人将他们转化为怀恨在心、贪婪成性的军队，他们对每一条小路都了如指掌。

sentences.en: They leave us as spies upon our posts and our strength, and they return upon us as guides and soldiers and incendiaries.
sentences.zh: 他们离开我们，充当刺探我们哨所和兵力的间谍，然后又作为向导、士兵和纵火犯回到我们身边。

sentences.en: A guy actually from the National Museum of American History, the Smithsonian, writes, Christopher Wilson.
sentences.zh: 史密森尼学会美国国家历史博物馆的一个家伙，克里斯托弗·威尔逊，写下了这样的话。

sentences.en: The irony is, the very point when Key is writing his poem about the land of the free,
sentences.zh: 具有讽刺意味的是，就在基伊写下关于自由之乡的诗篇的那一刻，

sentences.en: black African-American slaves are trying to escape the land of the free and to reach those British ships in Baltimore Harbor that are the antagonists of the poem.
sentences.zh: 黑人非洲裔美国奴隶正试图逃离自由之乡，去寻找巴尔的摩港中那些作为这首诗对立面的英国军舰。

sentences.en: And as to quote Christopher Wilson, this guy from the museum,
sentences.zh: 用博物馆这位专家克里斯托弗·威尔逊的话来说，

sentences.en: they knew that they were far more likely to find freedom and liberty under the Union Jack than they were under the Star Spangled Banner.
sentences.zh: 他们知道，在米字旗下找到自由和解放的可能性，远大于在星条旗下。

sentences.en: He sounds an excellent curator.
sentences.zh: 他听起来是个极好的馆长。

sentences.en: I commend him for his objectivity.
sentences.zh: 我赞赏他的客观性。

sentences.en: This is literally the best story we've ever done on this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这简直是我们在这个播客上做过的最好的故事。

sentences.en: Anyway, the war ends in 1815, basically in a draw, and Coburn is true to his word.
sentences.zh: 总之，战争在1815年结束，基本上打了个平手，科伯恩也兑现了他的诺言。

sentences.en: He now has about 6,000 escaped slaves, and the treaty called for the return of all United States property.
sentences.zh: 他现在大约有6000名逃跑的奴隶，而条约要求归还所有的美国财产。

sentences.en: So the Americans expected to get them back, and Coburn did not give them back.
sentences.zh: 所以美国人期望把他们要回来，但科伯恩没有把他们交出来。

sentences.en: Because everything has changed, because the British government is now committed to abolitionism.
sentences.zh: 因为一切都变了，因为英国政府现在致力于废奴主义。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, at least the abolition of the slave trade, let's say.
sentences.zh: 好吧，至少可以说是废除奴隶贸易。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So most of these people actually ended up in Canada.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人大多数最终去了加拿大。

sentences.en: But a lot of the colonial marines, so the people who had seen action, went to Trinidad.
sentences.zh: 但许多殖民地海军陆战队员，也就是那些参加过战斗的人，去了特立尼达。

sentences.en: This is an incredible story, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这是一个令人难以置信的故事。

sentences.en: They were given special villages under the command of their old sergeants.
sentences.zh: 他们在老中士的指挥下被分配了专门的村庄。

sentences.en: They settled there, and they were called Americans.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里定居，被称为“美国人”。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And they are still there today, and they're still called Americans.
sentences.zh: 他们今天依然在那里，并且仍然被称为“美国人”。

sentences.en: Goodness, that's amazing.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: It's an incredible story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个不可思议的故事。

sentences.en: Anyway, to go back to the words of Francis Scott Key's anthem,
sentences.zh: 无论如何，回到弗朗西斯·斯科特·基伊的国歌歌词，

sentences.en: No refuge could save the hireling and slave from the terror of flight or the gloom of the grave.
sentences.zh: “无论是雇佣兵还是奴隶，都无法在逃亡的恐惧或坟墓的黑暗中找到庇护。”

sentences.en: I think it is perfectly possible he is talking about these people whose flight has been such a big story.
sentences.zh: 我认为完全有可能他是在谈论这些人，他们的逃亡曾是一个如此宏大的故事。

sentences.en: He is saying, basically, we will catch up with you, or you will die.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在说，我们会追上你们，或者你们会死。

sentences.en: I mean, it works both ways, though, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 不过，我的意思是，这也可以从两方面来解读，不是吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, that's kind of maybe the...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这可能有点...

sentences.en: That's poetry.
sentences.zh: 这是诗歌。

sentences.en: Double meaning.
sentences.zh: 双关意涵。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: However, there's one other aspect.
sentences.zh: 然而，还有一个方面。

sentences.en: I said there were two reasons to think it was more complicated, and the other one is Key himself.
sentences.zh: 我说过有两条理由认为事情更复杂，另一个理由就是基伊本人。

sentences.en: Now, the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 现在，剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: Ever since we started the podcast, we've never been into cancelling people or setting ourselves up as hanging judges.
sentences.zh: 自从我们开始做这个播客以来，我们从来没有热衷于取消文化，也没有把自己打扮成严厉的法官。

sentences.en: However, I think as an outsider, you can see why black Americans might find it difficult to celebrate Francis Scott Key as an individual.
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为作为局外人，你可以理解为什么黑人美国人可能会觉得很难把弗朗西斯·斯科特·基伊作为一个个体来庆祝。

sentences.en: He has, at best, a very ambiguous attitude to slavery.
sentences.zh: 他对奴隶制的态度往好了说也非常暧昧。

sentences.en: He owned slaves himself.
sentences.zh: 他自己拥有奴隶。

sentences.en: He bought his first slave in 1800.
sentences.zh: 他在1800年买了他的第一个奴隶。

sentences.en: He owned six by 1820.
sentences.zh: 到1820年他拥有了六个。

sentences.en: When he died in 1843, he had eight.
sentences.zh: 当他在1843年去世时，他拥有八个。

sentences.en: He sometimes represented, as a lawyer, slave owners seeking the return of their property.
sentences.zh: 他有时作为律师代表寻求索回财产的奴隶主。

sentences.en: On the other hand, he did free some of his slaves.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，他确实释放了一些奴隶。

sentences.en: He represented slaves who sought their freedom.
sentences.zh: 他曾代表过寻求自由的奴隶。

sentences.en: And when a friend of his liberated his slaves in his will, Francis Scott Key was one of the executors, and he worked to get them their freedom.
sentences.zh: 当他的一个朋友在遗嘱中解放他的奴隶时，弗朗西斯·斯科特·基伊就是执行人之一，他为争取他们的自由而努力。

sentences.en: And was he doing this before he wrote this poem?
sentences.zh: 那他是在写这首诗之前做这件事的吗？

sentences.en: After, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想是在之后。

sentences.en: Maybe his attitudes evolved.
sentences.zh: 也许他的态度发生了演变。

sentences.en: Well, I think his attitudes are complicated.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他的态度很复杂。

sentences.en: He is a founder member and a very keen fundraiser for something called the American Colonization Society.
sentences.zh: 他是美国殖民协会的创始成员和非常积极的筹款人。

sentences.en: And the goal of the American Colonization Society is to send black men and women who have been freed to Africa.
sentences.zh: 美国殖民协会的目标是将获得自由的黑人男女送到非洲去。

sentences.en: And this is the project that actually culminates in the foundation of Liberia in 1847.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个最终在1847年促成利比里亚建立的项目。

sentences.en: Now, you may look at this and say, well, that's a very nice thing to do.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会看到这一点并说，这真是一件好事。

sentences.en: Actually, most of the people who backed this society were slaveholders.
sentences.zh: 事实上，支持这个协会的大多数人都是奴隶主。

sentences.en: It was particularly popular in Maryland.
sentences.zh: 它在马里兰州特别受欢迎。

sentences.en: It was particularly popular with the planter elite.
sentences.zh: 它在种植园精英阶层中特别受欢迎。

sentences.en: It's kind of generated by an anxiety that white and black Americans can never live together.
sentences.zh: 这某种程度上是由一种焦虑产生的，即白人和黑人美国人永远无法生活在一起。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly so.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: So it's complicated because on the one hand, these people would undoubtedly have said themselves, we're motivated by Christian charity.
sentences.zh: 所以这很复杂，因为一方面，这些人毫无疑问会自己说，我们是由基督教慈善心驱使的。

sentences.en: We want to find somewhere for these people to live.
sentences.zh: 我们想为这些人找个地方住。

sentences.en: We want to find them a home.
sentences.zh: 我们想为他们找个家。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the people who fundraise, the people who are activists for this society are often explicitly raciSt.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，筹款的人、这个协会的积极分子往往是明确的种族主义者。

sentences.en: They say, we're a white country.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们是一个白人国家。

sentences.en: We don't want free black men and women as citizens among us.
sentences.zh: 我们不希望获得自由的黑人男女成为我们当中的公民。

sentences.en: Get rid.
sentences.zh: 滚开。

sentences.en: Send them to Africa.
sentences.zh: 把他们送到非洲去。

sentences.en: And actually, a lot of abolitionists and a lot of black people themselves hate this colonization society because they see it as, I mean, they see it as unambiguously raciSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，许多废奴主义者和许多黑人自己都讨厌这个殖民协会，因为他们认为这——我的意思是，他们认为这是毫无疑问的种族主义。

sentences.en: As for abolitionism, Key is not a fan of abolitionism at all.
sentences.zh: 至于废奴主义，基伊一点也不喜欢废奴主义。

sentences.en: So you mentioned Nelson.
sentences.zh: 所以你提到了纳尔逊。

sentences.en: We talked about Nelson and slavery.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过纳尔逊和奴隶制。

sentences.en: Nelson's not a fan of abolitionism, but I don't think it's something that's on his mind very much.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊不是废奴主义的粉丝，但我认为这不是他很放在心上的事情。

sentences.en: He's not a fan of it because he thinks it will weaken the British Empire, its commerce, its trade, and all of this.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢它，是因为他认为这会削弱大英帝国、它的商业、贸易以及所有这些。

sentences.en: But Nelson never actively campaigns against abolitionism.
sentences.zh: 但纳尔逊从未积极反对过废奴主义。

sentences.en: Francis Scott Key does.
sentences.zh: 而弗朗西斯·斯科特·基伊则不然。

sentences.en: As district attorney for Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 作为华盛顿特区的地区检察官，

sentences.en: in the 1830s, he is a tireless foe of abolitionism.
sentences.zh: 在1830年代，他是废奴主义的不懈敌人。

sentences.en: He brings a libel case against one anti-slavery activist, a guy who had said, you know, there's no justice for black people in this town.
sentences.zh: 他对一名反奴隶制活动人士提起了一起诽谤诉讼，那家伙曾说过，你知道的，这个城镇里对黑人没有公正可言。

sentences.en: Key basically drove him out with this libel case.
sentences.zh: 基伊基本上通过这起诽谤诉讼把他赶走了。

sentences.en: Most famously, he prosecuted a guy from New York who was living in Georgetown merely for having a trunk full of anti-slavery tracts.
sentences.zh: 最著名的是，他起诉了一个来自纽约、住在乔治敦的家伙，仅仅因为他有一个装满反奴隶制小册子的皮箱。

sentences.en: Key accused him of seditious libel and inciting slaves and blacks to revolt.
sentences.zh: 基伊指控他犯有煽动性诽谤罪，并煽动奴隶和黑人起义。

sentences.en: And he tried to turn this case into a massive political set piece, I think because he wanted to use it to boost his own political career.
sentences.zh: 他试图把这起案件变成一场宏大的政治重头戏，我想是因为他想借此来提升自己的政治生涯。

sentences.en: Are you willing, gentlemen, he said in his closing speech, to abandon your country, to permit it to be taken from you and occupied by the abolitionist,
